title: Teaching Charles Mingus his first bass lessons
summary: Buddy Collette and Britt Woodman brought Mingus to him; Mingus practiced seventeen or eighteen hours a day.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Tell me about your association with Charlie Mingus. You taught him, right?
Yes, I was his original teacher. I started him on the bass.
How did he happen to come to you?

Buddy Collette and Britt Woodman. Oh, there's some guy who's calling me all the time now; he wants to do a movie about Mingus. Anyhow, Britt Woodman and Buddy Collette brought him to me. They had heard me playing, and they liked the sound I got out of the instrument and the approach to it. Because my inspiration had been Duke Ellington, so naturally I was conscious of where the beat was, and the rhythm... Anyhow, they brought him to me, and I got him started and showed him how to approach it. And to prove that genius is hard work, Mingus practiced 17 or 18 hours a day, every day. Well, I never practiced that long at the time, you know. I was playing the tuba and trying to write, or writing... You have to divide your time up. So that's really the secret of Mingus' greatness. He worked at it.
How old was Mingus? What year was this when he came to you?

The year would have been, I think, '39. '39 and '40, somewhere in there. Because I remember, my youngest daughter was born... She came along just in that period. I can't pin the exact date down. I probably could
if I really did some mental research. But I'd say it was between '38 and '40 when he started.
